title: Frag-rate-aware KV allocator with retention hysteresis and compaction throttler
creator: Luca Moretti
description:
Background: Our GPU KV cache suffers from transient fragmentation when continuous batching mixes short-lived and long-lived sequences. This ticket proposes a frag-rate-aware allocation strategy that combines per-allocation retention hysteresis, compaction throttling, and batching signals to reduce fragmentation while preserving tail latency SLOs.

Goals: Reduce reclaimable fragmentation by 30% under mixed workloads, limit compaction-induced latency spikes (p90 increase < 5%), and keep overall memory overhead <= 3% of baseline. Provide telemetry to steer heuristics and enable safe rollout via canary.

Proposed approach summary:
- Frag-rate telemetry: emit metrics per-GPU and per-pool (frag_rate, reclaimable_bytes, avg_kv_lifetime, eviction_churn_ratio). Use a 1m and 10m window to separate spikes from steady-state.
- Retention hysteresis: allocate KV slots with a lightweight lifetime score (short/medium/long) derived from request batch signals (sequence length, user-level cache hints) and observed reuse. Promote demoted slots on repeated hits. Hysteresis prevents oscillating evictions for borderline keys.
- Microzone placement: split large GPU pools into hot/mixed/cold microzones. Allocate small, frequently reused KV entries into hot microzones with tighter occupancy caps; less-frequently reused entries placed into cold zones where fragmentation is cheaper to compact.
- Compaction throttler: background compaction respects a dynamic budget calculated from current frag_rate and observed tail-latency headroom; compaction aggressiveness is scaled by reclaimable_bytes and limited by a per-GPU latency budget. Implements soft/hard watermarks for compaction start/stop.
- Continuous-batching integration: annotate requests with expected reuse horizon (from batching controller). Batching controller will provide an optional reuse_hint to allocator so that transient tokens from short-lived batches are preferentially placed/evicted.
- Eviction stabilization: introduce a short probabilistic cool-down for recently promoted keys to prevent immediate re-eviction when compaction finishes.

Trade-offs considered:
- More complex allocation logic increases scheduler CPU overhead; we limit cost by using bucketed lifetime scores (3 levels) and amortized placement decisions in the allocation fast path.
- Conservative compaction reduces fragmentation gains; the throttler targets periods with available latency headroom to perform heavier compaction.

Success criteria / acceptance criteria (see acceptance_criteria field for checklist): Rollout plan and rollback knobs exist, metrics show reduced fragmentation and acceptable tail latency, unit/integration tests and a canary run on dedicated cluster complete without regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Frag-rate telemetry available in Console for canary cluster (1m and 10m windows)
Automated integration test simulating mixed short/long sequence workload shows >=30% reduction in reclaimable fragmentation vs baseline
Compaction throttler honors latency budget: p90 latency regressions < 5% under a standard benchmark
Safe feature flag and config knobs: per-GPU compaction_budget_ms, hysteresis thresholds, microzone sizes
Canary rollout plan documented and executed with metrics dashboard and automated rollback on SLA breach
notes: 2026-02-15: RFC drafted and reviewed with runtime team. Identified need for batching controller signal – assigned to batching lead for API (see dependency ENG-31845).
2026-02-20: Prototype allocator module implemented in user-space allocator shim; initial microzone strategy validated in local perf harness (GH#5678).
2026-02-27: Telemetry schema finalized: frag_rate, reclaimable_bytes, avg_kv_lifetime, eviction_churn_ratio. Console UX hooks requested by product (PRD link in attachments).
2026-03-02: Integration with batching controller: reuse_hint stable API v1. Batching controller emits short/medium/long hint derived from sequence_length histogram. Patch GH#5911 opened for review.

2026-03-05: Early canary scheduled on staging-dedicated-03. Compaction throttler default config: soft_watermark=12% reclaimable, hard_watermark=25% reclaimable, compaction_budget_ms=15ms per GPU per minute. Monitoring dashboards prepared.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (prototype): implement frag-rate telemetry and retention hysteresis in allocator shim; expose metrics
Phase 2 (integration): consume reuse_hint from batching controller and implement microzone placement
Phase 3 (safety): compaction throttler with soft/hard watermarks and latency budget enforcement
Phase 4 (rollout): canary on staging-dedicated, observe metrics 48h, iterate thresholds
Phase 5 (GA): enable by default with conservative thresholds, monitor for 2 weeks before increasing aggressiveness
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Incorrect reuse_hint could misclassify long-lived keys -> Mitigation: fall back to observed reuse and promote demoted keys after repeated hits
Risk: Compaction causes latency spikes -> Mitigation: enforce strict per-GPU latency budget and automatic rollback if p95/p99 increase beyond configured thresholds
Risk: Increased CPU overhead for allocator -> Mitigation: keep fast-path allocation simple with 3-level buckets and only run expensive placement every N allocations
